Definition: from a derivative of G143; properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment:--senses.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Hebrews 5:14: strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. The word is the organ of perception — the senses themselves — and the writer says they are trained the way an athlete trains a muscle: by use.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse calls the senses a muscle trained by use, and the word itself carries little beyond that picture; its weight is Hebrews' training plan for maturity.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
